text: Stage 7 compares governed self-modification with an otherwise matched control that permits no self-modification, under a registration that predates observation.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Institutional Design for Governed Self-Modification in Agentic Reputation Architecture (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7694598

isBasedOn.name: Institutional Design for Governed Self-Modification in Agentic Reputation Architecture

abstract: The question is never whether agents can change. It is whether the change is visible, priced, and governed. Prohibition is undesirable and unenforceable, because the agents are software. The empirical contribution is a registered Stage 7 comparison of governed self-modification with a matched control, and its primary efficacy hypothesis was not supported. The run did not measure safety or behavioral drift, so the claim of improvement without added risk remains untested. The principal limitation is that no frontier-model agent was tested.
